I'ORFWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Soaps and Other Surface Active Agents Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Sodium tripolyphosphate (STPP) is generally used as a builder in detergent industry. Shce it causes eutrophication to the water sources thereby affecting the life of living organisms, there was intensive research for an alternative to STPP. After rigorous research and investigation, it was found that the zeolite is the most suitable and ideal replacement. .Zeolite is the main builder in most of the detergents two different ways: a) b) from amorphous and in many developed countries. It is synthesized normally in

hydrogels prepared from high purity sources of sodium silicates and sodium aluminates, followed by reaction with aqueous sodium hydroxide. l,.27H20

from kaolin by calcinations

The formula of zeolite, normally used by detergent industry is Na,2(A10,.Si0,)

.Zeolite is manufactured as zeolite slurry first and then spray dried to form zeolite powder. In the spray dried detergent manufacturing process, zeolite is used in the slurry form and spray drying in the zeolite plant is hence eliminated. Zeolite whenever dispatched in the slurry form is stabilized and sent under the nomenclature `Zeolite Mas[cr Batch'. Zeolite in powder form is used in detergent cakes and in detergent powders prepared by dry mixing process. In this standard r-equirement for both zeolite powder and slurry have been specified. There is no 1S0 standard on this subject. The composition of the Committee This standard has been prepared based on indigenous technology. for formulation of this standard is given in Annex K

responsible

For t!le purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 1S 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (rcwi.wd)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

S.1

Packing

The material shall be packed in dry steel tanks or barrels or HDPE/Paper or asagreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

5.2.1.1 `The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau ofIndian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 5.2 Marking

meter.

The zero adjustment

of the rdlectance

meter is first

done by placing the reflectance head on a black plate. Then the hundred adjustment is done by placing the reflectance head on a perfectly white magnesia block or barium sulphate crystals packed in a suitable cup. The instrument reading corresponds to the percentage of relative brightness.

ANNEX J (Clause 6)
SAMPLING J-1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS J-1.1 In drawing,
preparing, storing and handling samples, the following precautions shall be observed. J-1. 1.1 Samples shall be taken in a protected place, not exposed to damp air, dust or soot. J-1. 1.2 The sampling dry when used. instruments shall be clean and

OF ZEOLITE

DETERGENT

GRADE

J-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING J-2.1 Lot In a single consignment, all the packages containing material of the same type, and drawn from the same batch of manufacture, shall constitute a lot. J-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements prescribed in this stmdard, tests shall be carried out on each lot separately. The number (n) of
bags to be selected for drawing the sample shall depend upon the size (N) of the lot, and shall be in accordance with Table 2.

J-1.1.3 The samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instruments and the containers for samples shal I be protected from adventitious contamination. J-1.l.4 The samples shall be placed in clean and dry glass containers. The sample containers shall be of such a size that they are almost completely filled by the sample.

J-1.1.6 The samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the normal state and that they are protected from light. 6

J-4.1 Tests for the determination of active ingredient shall be performed on each of the individual samples. J-4.2 Tests for the determination of the remaining characteristics given in Table 1 shall be conducted on the composite sample. J-5 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY J-5.1 For Individual Samples
For the characteristic which has been determined on the individual sample, the mean (~.and the range (R) of test results shall be calculated as follows: Mean (X) = Sum of test results Number of test results Range (R) = Difference between the maximum and minimum values of test results.

J-3 PREPARATION OF GROSS SAMPLES, TEST SAMPLES AND REFERENCE SAMPLES J-3. 1 Gross Samples J-3. 1.1 From each one of the bags selected as in J-2, draw at random one or more containers. The material in the containers so choosen shall be nearly thrice the quantity required for purposes of test as indicated in J-4. J-3. 1.1.1 The material from the containers-selected as in J-3.1.1 shall be disintegrated, if necessary, and mixed thoroughly to give the gross sample for the bag. J-3.2 Test Samples J-3.2. 1 Segregate carefully the gross samples. From each gross sample, take a small but equal quantity of material and mix it thoroughly into a composite sample which should be of a size sufficient to carry out triplicate test for all the characteristics specified under J-4. The composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier, and the third for the referee. J-3.2.2 The remaining portion of the material in each one of the gross samples shall be divided into three equal parts, each forming an individual sample. One set of individual samples representing the n selected bags for the purchaser, another for the supplier, and the third for the referee. J-3.2.3 ,411the composite and individual samples shall be transferred to separate containers. These containers shall then be sealed airtight with stoppers, and Iabelled with full particulars of identification given in J-1.1.5. J-3.3 Reference Samples
